answer: The lantern cap is checked at intake and wander publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a farm in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, since every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a timber tag. That is 10 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
